title: The operator deploys an environment from the goal and sees where it went
description:
SPIDR child 3 of task-5d30948435524c6fa2789e1c033aafe7 (architect-20a6d1eb, 2026-09-05). dependsOn child 1 (task-3706b7e7bb8741d88105f42c25166ea0) and child 2 (task-04b3ce7e349743c2a156d32ee5550ba5). PROOF ROW: owns the UI, the Playwright journey, the live drive and the docs (global rail 21).

WHAT THIS ROW OWNS: a Deployments card on the opened goal (per environment: target, last deploy sha / time / url / status, Deploy arm/confirm), the release-receipt row on Runs, Needs-you listing a goal ready to deploy after preview/release, and the live local deploy.

THE CARD MUST NOT INVITE AN ACCIDENTAL PRODUCTION DEPLOY. PREVIEW and PRODUCTION sit on the same card, and the destructive one is a click away from the safe one. Arm/confirm (the PUBLISH card's pattern) is the minimum; make the environment being deployed unmistakable in the confirm step, and show whether a release decision exists for a PRODUCTION deploy so the operator sees what child 2 recorded rather than discovering it in a receipt afterwards.

MEASURED AT HEAD (branch moe/work-2026-09-04) by architect-20a6d1eb: the pattern to model is apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/goal-publish.tsx (141 lines, testids cr.publish.root/landed/state/link/unoffered) with publish-port.ts (22 lines) spending the offer through offer-wire's `spendOffer`. Needs-you is needs-you-model.ts (its NEEDS_YOU_KINDS roster at :28) plus needs-you.tsx. Note other rows are extending both: task-a988ca1c adds PLAN_REJECTED and task-33ceae56 adds a preview card - expect a rebase on that roster.
definitionOfDone: The Deployments card renders per environment - target, last deploy sha, time, url and status - with a Deploy arm/confirm modelled on the PUBLISH card, dispatching child 2's kinds through offer-wire `spendOffer` (no second decision wire).

THE CONFIRM STEP NAMES THE ENVIRONMENT UNMISTAKABLY, and a PRODUCTION deploy shows whether a release decision exists on the goal. Assert both: PREVIEW and PRODUCTION share a card, and the operator must not be able to deploy production believing they clicked preview.

The card is ABSENT (not a dead button) when the daemon offers no deploy, and a missing target renders DEPLOY_TARGET_MISSING as words with a way to set one. All four refusal codes render VERBATIM, with DEPLOY_BUILD_FAILED carrying the tool's last stderr line so a failure is diagnosable from the browser.
Runs shows deploy receipts and Needs-you lists a goal ready to deploy, then stops listing it once deployed - assert appearance AND disappearance.

A Playwright journey against a REAL daemon (with a fake docker port behind the daemon) covers target -> deploy -> url; `pnpm test:e2e:browser` count line quoted. Control-room fixtures are REAL daemon frames from that run.

LIVE DRIVE: the PREVIEW environment deployed LOCALLY with docker for UnAI or the scaffold app - the receipt and a curl of the health URL (status and body) in a row comment under ~4500 chars. If docker is unavailable on the lane, record DEPLOY_DOCKER_UNAVAILABLE verbatim rather than a fabricated deploy.

The runbook gains a 'Deploy' section and README's Stage 2 status is updated to the measured state, with the live drive's date. Gates quoted with count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test:e2e:browser`.
taskRails: PRODUCTION IS ONE CLICK FROM PREVIEW ON THIS CARD. The confirm step names the environment unmistakably; this is the row's one safety property.
THIS ROW PROVES, IT DOES NOT REBUILD: an infrastructure defect is child 1's, a deploy-effect defect is child 2's. Comment there and report_blocked.
REUSE the PUBLISH card's arm/confirm shape and offer-wire `spendOffer`. A second decision wire is a design regression.
NEEDS_YOU_KINDS is being extended by two other rows concurrently (task-a988ca1c, task-33ceae56) - rebase, do not delete a peer's entry.
ASCII-only sources and apostrophe-free JSX text (scheduler package-boundary scan); check any new testid namespace is free; keep every production file under 250 lines.
